translationRepairs: The Chinese heading is 〈（吉禮六）〉; the English closing 〉 is an unmatched CJK title bracket, and removing it leaves an accurate rendering.
The same stray 〉 appears in the literal field and is not required once （吉禮六） is given in English parentheses.

In the first year of Xuande, after Taizong had been enshrined in the ancestral temple, the Prince of Zheng Zhu Zhan’en was again sent to the Hall of Ancestors to set out wine and fruit, announce the sacrifice, and install the spirit seat.

In the first year of Xuande, after Taizong had been enshrined in the ancestral temple, the Prince of Zheng Zhu Zhanzhan was again sent to the Hall of Ancestors to set out wine and fruit, announce the sacrifice, and install the spirit seat.
鄭王瞻颭 names the prince 瞻颭, romanized Zhanzhan; Zhan’en does not match those characters.

In the first year of Xuande, after Taizong was enshrined in the ancestral temple, the Prince of Zheng Zhu Zhan’en was again dispatched to the Hall of Ancestors to set out wine and fruit for a sacrificial announcement and to install the spirit seat in peace.

In the first year of Xuande, after Taizong was enshrined in the ancestral temple, the Prince of Zheng Zhu Zhanzhan was again dispatched to the Hall of Ancestors to set out wine and fruit for a sacrificial announcement and to install the spirit seat in peace.
The literal line repeats Zhu Zhan’en for 瞻颭; Zhanzhan is the matching romanization.
The bier-bearers numbered as many as a thousand, and all along the route they demanded whatever they wished.
The boat-haulers numbered as many as a thousand, and all along the route they demanded whatever they wished.
In the memorial about 南京進鮮船, 輓夫 are the boats’ haulers or trackers, not funeral bier-bearers.
The bearers of the bier reached a thousand men, and along the route they extorted everything.
The boat-haulers reached a thousand men, and along the route they extorted everything.
The literal ‘bearers of the bier’ likewise misreads 輓夫 on the tribute-boat route.
In the eighteenth year the death anniversaries of Gaozu and his empress were transferred to the Jingshen Hall, and those of Wenzong and his empress and the rest to the Yongxiao Hall.
In the eighteenth year the death anniversaries of Gaozu and his empress were transferred to the Jingshen Hall, and those of the Wen Emperor and his empress and the rest to the Yongxiao Hall.
文皇帝 is the Wen Emperor (Chengzu’s designation), not the temple name Wenzong.
In the eighteenth year the death anniversaries of Gaozu and his empress were moved to the Jingshen Hall, and those of Wenzong and his empress and below to the Yongxiao Hall.
In the eighteenth year the death anniversaries of Gaozu and his empress were moved to the Jingshen Hall, and those of the Wen Emperor and his empress and below to the Yongxiao Hall.
The literal Wenzong is the same misidentification of 文皇帝.
When Xiaozong took the throne, he posthumously honored his mother, Consort Ji, as Empress Xiaomu and enshrined her at Maoling.
When Xiaozong took the throne, he posthumously honored his mother, Consort Ji, as Empress Xiaomu and had her jointly buried at Maoling.
祔葬茂陵 is companion burial at Maoling; the following 不得祔廟 shows this is not tablet enshrinement.
The Spring and Autumn Annals records “the palace of Zhongzi, the younger wife”; Hu Anguo’s commentary says: “When Mencius entered Duke Hui’s temple, Zhongzi had no place for sacrifice.”
The Spring and Autumn Annals records “the palace of Zhongzi, the younger wife”; Hu Anguo’s commentary says: “When Lady Meng entered Duke Hui’s temple, Zhongzi had no place for sacrifice.”
In Hu Anguo’s Chunqiu comment, 孟子 is Duke Hui’s principal wife Lady Meng, not the philosopher Mencius.
The Spring and Autumn Annals records “the palace of Zhongzi, the younger wife”; Hu Anguo’s commentary says: “When Mencius entered Duke Hui’s temple, Zhongzi had no place for sacrifice.”
The Spring and Autumn Annals records “the palace of Zhongzi, the younger wife”; Hu Anguo’s commentary says: “When Lady Meng entered Duke Hui’s temple, Zhongzi had no place for sacrifice.”
The literal Mencius is the same error in this no-double-matching precedent.
The commentators say: ‘Closest means the mother born to the uncle.’
The commentators say: ‘Closest means the birth mother of the husband’s father.’
舅所生母 is the husband’s father’s birth mother among the 祖姑, not a mother borne by an uncle; the proposed parenthesis is unnecessary.
The commentators say: ‘Closest means the mother born to the uncle.’
The commentators say: ‘Closest means the birth mother of the husband’s father.’
The literal field has the same 舅所生母 error; a shorter kinship gloss is accurate without the extra parenthesis.
The Grand Mentor Shi Bao and others also said it could not be done.
The Supervisor of the Household of the Heir Apparent Shi Bao and others also said it could not be done.
詹事 is the Supervisor of the Household of the Heir Apparent, not Grand Mentor; the proposed short title omits the heir-apparent household.

In the fourth month of the fourth year, Yuan had already been appointed acting vice director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and again memorialized requesting establishment of an Eternal Chamber and exalted sacrifice to the imperial father in the Grand Temple; Minister of Rites Xi Shu and others deliberated: “The Son of Heaven has seven temples; Zhou Wen and Wu both had merit and virtue, and therefore established the Wen and Wu Eternal Chambers above the three zhao and three mu.

In the fourth month of the fourth year, Yuan had already been appointed vice director of a bureau of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and again memorialized requesting establishment of an Eternal Chamber and exalted sacrifice to the imperial father in the Grand Temple; Minister of Rites Xi Shu and others deliberated: “The Son of Heaven has seven temples; Zhou Wen and Wu both had merit and virtue, and therefore established the Wen and Wu Eternal Chambers above the three zhao and three mu.
光祿寺署丞 is the assistant director of a bureau in that court; 署 here is the bureau, not an ‘acting’ prefix.
Soon thereafter Left Sublector Jiang Rubi requested moving the imperial father’s temple to the head of the mu temples, to serve as the future Eternal Chamber, standing alongside Chengzu’s temple.
Soon thereafter Left Mentor Jiang Rubi requested moving the imperial father’s temple to the head of the mu temples, to serve as the future Eternal Chamber, standing alongside Chengzu’s temple.
左庶子 is Left Mentor, not the nonce title Sublector.
Right Supporter Guo Xiyan also wished, outside Taizu’s temple and Wen’s Eternal Chamber, to establish only four parental temples and remove Xiaozong and Wuzong from the line.
Right Adviser Guo Xiyan also wished, outside Taizu’s temple and Wen’s Eternal Chamber, to establish only four parental temples and remove Xiaozong and Wuzong from the line.
右贊善 is Right Adviser, not Supporter.

The Chinese names four brothers—南昌王、霍丘王、下蔡王、安豐王—then two consorts; the extra Huoqiu prince is invented and 下蔡 is Xiacai.

In the fourteenth year of Wanli, Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Pei Yingzhang said: “The princes were originally attached as collateral joint offerings to the ancestors.
從祖祔食, followed by 四祖之廟已祧, means the princes were ancillary joint offerings with the ancestors, not specifically the great-grandfather.
